subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off per-agent approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and what timeout/fail/proceed behavior should it use?
rationale: The missing behavior is real in current source, but solving it adds config surface and changes the reliability-versus-control contract for provider fallback routing.

options.title: Define the per-agent approval contract
options.body: Adopt a narrow default-off schema such as `agents.list[].model.requireApprovalBeforeFallback` with explicit timeout and fail/proceed semantics, then implement it with docs and upgrade-safe tests.

options.title: Keep automatic fallback only
options.body: Reject fallback approval as too much runtime friction and close this tracker after documenting that model visibility should use response prefixes and logs instead.

options.title: Defer to a broader approval-routing RFC
options.body: Leave this open but block implementation until approval routing, channel UX, and model fallback policy are designed together.

recommendation.title: Define the per-agent approval contract
recommendation.body: Adopt a narrow default-off schema such as `agents.list[].model.requireApprovalBeforeFallback` with explicit timeout and fail/proceed semantics, then implement it with docs and upgrade-safe tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant fallback and config schema history points most strongly to steipete for product-level model fallback contract decisions.
